paragraphs.text: Native VS Code client for DeepSeek Harness. Same workspace, same session, same agent runtime — VS Co
de and the browser share one Harness session.
DeepSeek Harness Connector for VS Code
Same Harness. Same Workspace. Same Session.

Your agent keeps running wherever it already is. This puts a native VS Code client in front of it:
a

ttach to the Harness on this machine, read the session the browser is reading, answer its
approvals,
and review every edit in VS Code's own diff.
English | 简体中文

Install ·
Open VSX ·
Download VSIX ·
Changelog ·
How it got built
An independent, unofficial community project — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or published by Dee
ependent, unofficial community project — not affiliated with, endorsed by, or published by DeepSeek.
*The 30-second trailer, cut down to its two product beats. The silence is deliberate — there is no n
arration, the film says it in type. Play it · How it got built (中文版: STORY.zh-CN.md)*
## What it does
- **Continues the session you already have.** Workspaces and sessions are read from the running Host

. Refresh that session in a browser and you see exactly what VS Code sent.
- **Answers approvals and
agent questions — for the conversation you are looking at.** Both waterfalls are settled by this pl
ugin, so a run is never blocked on a browser tab you have closed. The Host forwards every session's
waterfalls down one socket, so a card is drawn only when the frame names *your* session; a question
raised in a browser tab on another session is not rendered here, and switching to that session bring

s it back.
- **Reports what each turn changed, and can undo it — one hunk at a time.** Fed by the Ho
st's own turn record, so it covers a file a shell command edited, not only what a file tool reported
. Each hunk has its own undo; the file-level undo reverts whatever is left. Both check the file's cu

rrent bytes first and refuse rather than overwriting you.
- **Right-click to ask about things.** Sel
ect code, a file in the explorer, or a change in the diff editor and the context menu offers *Explai
n / Fix / Review* — pre-filled with a prompt and the right `@` mention, including the line range for

a selection.
- **Opens VS Code's own editor for anything that is code.** A diff is a real diff edit

or; a path opens the file. Nothing is reimplemented in the webview.
- **Finds the Host by itself**,
including the desktop app, which starts its Host on an OS-assigned port that changes on every launch

.
- **Four ways to obtain a session, and the default picks for you.** Mint one from the harness's ow
n credential store (zero configuration, but it means reading a file that also holds your API keys),
let the extension start `dsh web` and take the launch URL it prints, or paste a launch URL yourself.
`auto` — the default since v0.2.8 — does the first and falls back to the second. See How the sessio

n is obtained.
- **Starts no process unless you ask it to.** The default attaches to the Host you al

ready have running.
[该节后续省略]
## What's new in v0.4.1
**Pick the model in the editor, and prove "Open Web UI" works without opening a browser.**
Two changes landed. Model and thinking-depth selection now lives in VS Code — a `model ▾` / `thinkin
g ▾` bar under the composer, and a Model group in the ⚙ Settings panel, both going through the Host'
s `session/selectModel` and persisting as a durable `model/selection` event. And `npm run verify-web
ui` mints a cookie through the extension's own `BrowserSessionAuth` and hits the live Host: `401` wi
th no cookie, `200` with the minted one — a one-command end-to-end check instead of trusting the uni
ookie, `200` with the minted one — a one-command end-to-end check instead of trusting the unit test.
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

- VS Code ≥ 1.85
- A local `dsh web` (default port `3080`), either already running or started for yo

u by the default `sessionMode: "auto"`.
- The Harness must be on **the same machine as the VS Code w
indow**. That is the one hard constraint; Remote development covers what it means for Remote-SSH, WS
the one hard constraint; Remote development covers what it means for Remote-SSH, WSL and containers.
## Limitations

- **Loopback only.** The plugin talks to a Harness on the same machine, and the Host
itself binds lo

opback — see Remote development for the four
scenarios, including the three this machine could not e

xercise.
- **Under `sessionMode: "credentials"` the extension can read a file that contains your
API

keys.** It has to, to mint the session cookie — which is why that mode is no
longer the only one. S

ee How the session is obtained.
- **Managed launch only covers "nothing is listening".** A Host some

body else started —
a terminal, the desktop app — never shows us its launch URL, so that case still

ends in
the `paste` route. The two cover different halves and neither replaces the other.
- **The Ho

st started by `managed` is stopped when the window closes.** That is deliberate
(a stray Host holdin

g a port is exactly the mess this extension avoids), but it means
the Web UI tab you had open stops

working when you quit VS Code.
- **Managed launch needs a `dsh` that can actually boot.** An out-of-

date global `dsh` can
be too old for the credential file the desktop app wrote, and it will exit on

startup —
the panel's advice in that case is to open the log, because the reason is always in the
ch

ild's own last lines. Updating it fixes it. A `dsh` that is *missing* is a different
ending: managed

launch retries through `npx` first, and only if that also fails does it
offer to install one for yo

u.
- **Images depend on the model.** Whether a model accepts images is not published in `session/mod
elCatalog`, so the plugin can only pass the host's verdict through: a non-vision model fails the pro
mpt with `MODEL_DOES_NOT_SUPPORT_IMAGES`, and the panel tells you to switch models in Controls. Your

staged attachments are kept for the retry.
- **Staged files are process-bound.** An upload receipt
is tied to the session *and* the running `dsh web` process, so a file staged across a host restart m

ust be re-picked.
- History loads the last ~50 messages; "load older" is a future feature.
- **"Open

Web UI" can only add a token the extension was given.** Two of the three session
